title: Bidirectional A* in Alfama: meet-in-the-middle routes
description: Watch Bidirectional A* crawl Lisbon’s winding street graph from start and goal, converging faster than a one-way search. The visualization highlights how two coordinated frontiers shrink the search space in real-world mapping.
ig_caption:
🚦 Lisbon (Alfama) streets, but make it algorithmic. 

🧠✨ Bidirectional A* runs two informed searches at once: one forward from the start and one backward from the destination, each using a heuristic to estimate remaining cost. When the two frontiers meet, the route is stitched together—effectively a “meet-in-the-middle” strategy that can cut down explored nodes. 

🗺️ In graph terms: we treat the street network as a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges with distances), then search for the lowest-cost path. With consistent heuristics, Bidirectional A* balances exploration efficiency and optimality, making it especially compelling on dense real street maps like Alfama’s irregular grid. 

🔥 Want a version using traffic weights, turn penalties, or elevation costs? Comment “ELEVATION” and I’ll generate the next reel!
